title: Component template + theme column, v2
description: v2 lesson baked in: character lives in structure and content formatting, not only CSS. Rows carry a channel: 'css' rows compile to stylesheet rules; 'config' rows compile to the skeleton component's per-theme configuration and are VALIDATED against the skeleton's declared parameter enums — a cell value the skeleton cannot express fails the build; 'info' rows exist for the panel (behavior, slots, states documentation). No component may inherit its skeleton from any design system: the skeleton implements this template's union.

skeletonParams.description: The skeleton's declared parameters and their allowed values. config-row cells must match, or the generator fails: this is the expressibility gate.

row.description: NAMING RULE: one row is one ATTRIBUTE — an addressable characteristic of a part, in a state, belonging to one of the six pieces. 'Attribute' is the term for the row itself (do not say 'token' — that means a resolved value; do not say 'attribute' when you mean a DOM data-* hook — always say 'data attribute' for those to avoid collision).

id.description: Grammar: <piece>.<part>[.<subpart>].<property>[@state]. Examples: style.day.font, style.day.background@hover, structure.today-marker, behavior.range-selection, prop.density. piece = which of the six sections; part(s) = anatomy location, narrowest last; optional @state narrows to one interaction state.

param.description: config rows: which skeletonParams key this row sets

byDensity.description: density name -> slot -> value; only for systems with a density capability

provenance.description: slot or cell id -> source file/token in the DS clone
